findings.title: WMI-Spawned PowerShell Execution with Anti-Forensics
findings.description: WmiPrvSE.exe (PID 2876, NT Authority) spawned powershell.exe (PID 8712) executing as 'spsql' (Domain Admins). WMI invoked remotely with explicit spsql credentials. Attacker wiped cmdline of PS 8712 (args='-') to prevent forensic recovery.

findings.title: Two-Stage PowerShell Chain via SysWOW64 Remoting Mode
findings.description: 64-bit PS (PID 8712) spawned 32-bit SysWOW64 PS (PID 5848) with '-Version 5.1 -s -NoLogo -NoProfile' enabling remoting server mode and 32-bit execution context for shellcode loading.

findings.title: Staged Payload: p.exe in \Windows\Temp\Perfmon\
findings.description: Attacker payload staged at c:\windows\temp\perfmon\p.exe, masquerading as Windows Performance Monitor tooling. File and directory confirmed in filescan. Four distinct rundll32 prefetch hashes corroborate repeated shellcode execution.

findings.title: rundll32.exe Abuse for In-Memory Shellcode Loading
findings.description: Nine blank-cmdline rundll32.exe processes spawned from attacker processes (6 from PS 5848, 3 from p.exe 8260). Short lifespans (3-31 seconds) and no command-line arguments indicate shellcode injection use, not legitimate DLL loading.

findings.title: C2 Beaconing to 172.16.4.10:8080
findings.description: Nine+ TCP connections from subject host to 172.16.4.10:8080 (1 ESTABLISHED, 6 CLOSE_WAIT, 2+ CLOSED). Non-standard port, recurring pattern, and dissociation from live PIDs indicate C2 framework beaconing through an internal relay host.

findings.title: SMB Lateral Movement to 172.16.4.5 and 172.16.7.15
findings.description: Two ESTABLISHED outbound SMB connections to internal hosts. With Domain Admin context, these enabled full SMB-based lateral movement.

findings.title: Domain Admin Account 'spsql' Compromised
findings.description: Attack chain executes entirely as 'spsql' (SQL service account) which is a member of Domain Admins. Full domain-wide compromise impact.

findings.title: Code Injection in p.exe: 1.9MB Private RWX VAD
findings.description: 1.9MB PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE private memory region (no file backing) in p.exe. Consistent with reflective shellcode or staged C2 implant allocation.

findings.title: subject_srv.exe = F-Response Collection Agent (NOT Malicious)
findings.description: subject_srv.exe (PID 1096) is the F-Response Subject software used to acquire this memory image. Confirmed by command-line flags and port 3262 connection to forensic collection host.

findings.title: Hands-on-Keyboard Attacker Session Confirmed
findings.description: conhost.exe (PID 1740) spawned as direct child of attacker's powershell.exe (PID 8712) at the same timestamp, confirming an interactive console session — a human operator, not an automated script.

findings.title: WinRM Connection to 172.16.5.21
findings.description: CLOSED WinRM (5985) connection to 172.16.5.21. Insufficient to confirm successful authentication from memory alone.

findings.title: LDAP Enumeration of 172.16.4.4
findings.description: CLOSED LDAP connection to 172.16.4.4:389. Consistent with AD enumeration but unconfirmed from memory alone.

findings.title: External HTTPS to 52.16.55.11:443
findings.description: CLOSED external HTTPS connection. Could be C2 staging or routine traffic. Requires enrichment.

findings.title: Inbound SMB from 172.16.6.14
findings.description: ESTABLISHED inbound SMB from same subnet. Cannot confirm attacker pivot vs. legitimate admin.

findings.title: OUTLOOK.EXE Malfind Hits — RETRACTED (False Positive)
findings.description: Both RWX regions in OUTLOOK.EXE (PID 8128) begin with bytes 64 74 72 52 (dtrR), a known Outlook memory allocation signature. Not malicious. Retracted during self-correction.
